_about: Cloudflare edge config for the (future) PUBLIC rpc-latency dashboard. See docs/public-hardening.md.
_status: NOT applied by anything in this repo. An operator (or Terraform cloudflare_ruleset) applies these to the public zone deliberately. Nothing here flips anything public.

_placeholders.DASHBOARD_HOSTNAME: friendly public hostname, e.g. rpclatency.solana.org (set by ops at apply time)
_placeholders.DASHBOARD_PATH_PREFIX: /public-dashboards/ for a Grafana public dashboard (Option A); adjust for snapshots

_apply.managed_ruleset: Also enable the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset and Bot Fight Mode in the dashboard / via API (see _bot_mitigation).
_apply.note: Apply each phase's rules in a single PUT. Replace placeholders first.

rules.description: Allow only safe read methods to the public dashboard host

rules._note: Proxied-CNAME routing only: Grafana public dashboards render client-side and fetch panel data from /api/public/dashboards/<token>/query and /annotations. This allow rule must precede the broad /api/ block below, or those data fetches return 403 and the dashboard renders blank. Harmless under the Redirect Rule routing option (the public never hits DASHBOARD_HOSTNAME for /api/), but required for the proxied-CNAME option in docs/public-hardening.md Layer 2.
rules.description: Allow Grafana public-dashboard data API (panel queries/annotations) needed under proxied-CNAME routing

rules._note: The /d/ and /dashboards prefixes (and the broad /api/ block) prevent navigation to other dashboards and the admin/query API. Under proxied-CNAME routing the allow rule above must run first so /api/public/dashboards/ still passes. Under the Redirect Rule option none of these paths reach DASHBOARD_HOSTNAME, so the block is pure defense-in-depth.
rules.description: Block Grafana API / admin / auth / datasource paths from the public host
rules.expression: (http.host eq "DASHBOARD_HOSTNAME") and (starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/api/") or starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/admin/") or starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/login") or starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/logout") or starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/explore") or starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/datasources") or starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/d/") or starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/dashboards"))

rules.description: Block any request to the raw metrics path at the edge (defense in depth; /metrics is localhost-only on the origin)
Challenge automated/unverified bots while allowing verified good bots
rules.expression: (http.host eq "DASHBOARD_HOSTNAME") and (cf.client.bot) and not (cf.verified_bot_category in {"Search Engine Crawler" "Monitoring & Analytics"})

rules._note: Key is ip.src + cf.colo.id, so the mitigation applies per IP per PoP. Offices, mobile carriers, and university networks share one egress IP, so we use managed_challenge (not block) and a short 120s timeout to avoid locking out legitimate shared-IP viewers for 10 minutes after one occupant crosses the threshold. Genuinely abusive clients fail the challenge; humans pass it.
rules.description: Per-IP rate limit on the public dashboard host

rules._note: Effective only under the proxied-CNAME routing option, where dashboard payloads traverse DASHBOARD_HOSTNAME. Under the Redirect Rule option, DASHBOARD_HOSTNAME returns a 301/302 and the /public-dashboards/, /public/, and /avatar/ responses are served by Grafana's CDN (rpclatency.grafana.net) and never reach this rule, so only the redirect is cached, not the dashboard content. Do not assume burst protection from edge caching when using the redirect approach.
rules.description: Edge-cache dashboard responses briefly so viewer bursts collapse to a single origin fetch
rules.expression: (http.host eq "DASHBOARD_HOSTNAME") and (starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "DASHBOARD_PATH_PREFIX") or starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/public/") or starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/avatar/"))

_bot_mitigation.bot_fight_mode: Enable Bot Fight Mode (or Super Bot Fight Mode on Pro+). On Pro+, set verified-bots = allow, definitely-automated = managed_challenge.
_bot_mitigation.managed_ruleset: Enable the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset (and OWASP Core Ruleset if on a plan that includes it) on this zone.
_bot_mitigation.tls: SSL/TLS mode Full (strict); enable Always Use HTTPS and HSTS on the hostname.
